idiom_name: serial DispatchQueue (FIFO) or actor serial executor
implementation_notes: Swift's nearest point-to-point channel is a serial DispatchQueue: dispatch queues are FIFO queues of work items and the serial variant executes them one at a time in FIFO order, so a consumer loop over a serial queue gets the one-handler-per-item contract without locks. With Swift concurrency the actor is the modern equivalent - actor methods run on the actor's SerialExecutor, so its state is processed serially - and both are in-memory, meaning a broker or persistent store is required for durability across restarts.
pitfalls: DispatchQueue.sync onto the main queue deadlocks (documented) - the same trap applies when a queue synchronizes onto itself.
A concurrent queue is not a point-to-point channel: it starts work in FIFO order but completes out of order, so only serial queues and actors give the one-at-a-time contract.
Actor reentrancy: an await inside an actor method lets other messages interleave, so state invariants must be re-checked after every suspension.
